clue.text: Out on a limb

parts.note: the phrase usually means isolated and exposed, but read literally it is a cricket batsman dismissed because the ball struck a leg rather than the bat

explanation.surface: Someone left isolated and exposed, with no support for their position.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'out on a limb' (in a risky position) hides the cricket reading: a batsman is out when a leg, the limb, blocks a ball that would have hit the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a mode of dismissal where the batsman's leg stops a ball heading for the stumps, so the player is out because of a limb.

clue.text: Job one doesn't hate doing

parts.note: a task you would never hate, read as work undertaken for affection rather than pay

explanation.surface: A piece of work that someone actually enjoys rather than resents.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means work done for pleasure or devotion, not reward, so it is a job one is happy to do.

clue.text: Cheese from town in Indian district

annotationWithheld.why: Cheese from town in Indian district (5): GOUDA is a cheese named after a Dutch town, but no clue word supplies the UD that would go inside GOA, and no search found the intended parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Cheese from town in Indian district

clue.text: Hoped norm could become a more rounded individual

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could become something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hoped the usual standard would turn into a more well-rounded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges HOPED NORM. 'More rounded' looks like 'well-rounded' in character, but it means plumper in build.
explanation.definitionFit: In body typing, this is the heavy, soft, round-bodied physique, as opposed to lean or muscular types.

clue.text: I hope Ida, despite losing energy, tamed snakes

indicators.note: tamed suggests the letters are brought under control and reordered
losing means a letter is dropped from the words before rearranging

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A woman called Ida, though tired out, managed to tame some serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes the E (energy) from I HOPE IDA, leaving IHOPIDA, and 'tamed' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological name for the suborder of reptiles containing serpents, used in the clue as a plural noun.

clue.text: One cannot hear a sound out of it

definitions.text: One cannot hear a sound out of it

parts.words: One cannot hear a sound out of it
parts.note: reads like a silent object, but means being beyond the distance at which noises can be heard

explanation.surface: Something so quiet that no noise ever comes from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the range within which one can hear; anyone outside that range hears nothing.

clue.text: Lazy person I had left about to get up

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived 'regarding', about

explanation.surface: A lazy person admits they left it late and are about to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns RE into ER, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who avoids work and passes time doing nothing.

clue.text: Kept a dog at home perhaps

definitions.text: Kept a dog at home perhaps

parts.words: Kept a dog at home perhaps
parts.note: sounds like owning a pet, but describes a dog housed in its own little shelter

explanation.surface: Someone kept a pet dog in the house, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: To be housed in a dog's hut or boarding establishment, the dog's home, is to have been put in one.

clue.text: Not free to jump

explanation.surface: Someone tied down and unable to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up or obliged means not free; a leap or spring is also this word, as in leaps and spring forward.

clue.text: Shooting injured fish

parts.note: hurt means injured
ling is a long-bodied fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A hunter firing at a fish he has wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' tempts as gunfire, but it means rushing, as in shooting past.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting along means moving very fast, rushing headlong.

clue.text: Tell martinet about violation

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and scattered

explanation.surface: Report a strict disciplinarian for breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TELL MARTINET; a martinet is a strict disciplinarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Abuse or cruel handling is a violation of someone's rights or person.

clue.text: Henry leaves uninjured despite being defenceless

indicators.note: leaves means goes out of the word, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: unharmed means uninjured
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry walks away unhurt even though he had no weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes H (henry, the SI unit) out of UNHARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons, a person has no means of defence.

clue.text: He will include raw material for research station

indicators.note: include means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: he'll is the contraction of he will

indicators.note: material suggests raw stuff worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man promises to bring raw materials for a scientific laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is the anagram signal, as raw stuff gets reworked; 'include' is the container signal. The site in Oxfordshire was Britain's atomic research establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: This Oxfordshire site was the home of Britain's Atomic Energy Research Establishment, a famous research centre.

clue.text: He has won round hesitantly

indicators.note: round suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A man who has, with some hesitation, been persuaded to agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the anagram signal. 'He has' looks like part of a sentence, but it is the definition: a possessor is one who has.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is one who has something, so 'he has' describes the holder.

clue.text: Was acquainted with, say, country state

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, and its sound is what counts

parts.note: knew means was acquainted with
Mexico is a country in North America

explanation.surface: Someone knew a land and its regions, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for the sound of KNEW, which is NEW; then add MEXICO.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the southwest, bordering its southern neighbour.

clue.text: George, vehicle navigator

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a vehicle
a pilot steers or navigates a ship or plane

explanation.surface: George, the person who drives and directs the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' looks like a man's name, but it is old airmen's slang for the automatic flight system.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots nicknamed the automatic steering system of an aircraft 'George'.

clue.text: Old chief writer to continue slowly and tediously

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
drag on means to continue slowly and tediously

explanation.surface: An ancient leader is an author who goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: The title belonged to ancient British chieftains, most famously Uther, father of King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend this was the title of an ancient British war leader, a supreme chief.

clue.text: Service building in the valley?

parts.note: a place of worship sitting low in a valley, read as the evangelical, plain wing of Anglican worship

explanation.surface: A chapel standing in a valley where services are held.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Anglican tradition favouring simple, evangelical worship, punningly a place of worship placed low down.

clue.text: Need student to leave garden trowel out for senecio jacobaea!

indicators.note: out suggests the remaining letters are put out of order

parts.note: the word need is taken as written
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool tossed aside in favour of a weed's Latin name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges what is left of GARDEN TROWEL once the letters of NEED and an L (learner) have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Senecio jacobaea is the botanical name of the common yellow-flowered weed toxic to horses.

clue.text: Principal ready for receiver

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A school principal prepared to take a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests a school head and 'receiver' a telephone; the receiver is worn over the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones with a microphone, a device for receiving sound.

clue.text: What joggers use their elbows for

definitions.text: What joggers use their elbows for

parts.words: What joggers use their elbows for
parts.note: runners pumping their arms, read instead as people jogging someone with an elbow

explanation.surface: How runners use their arms while out for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone is to give a gentle push with the elbow, a prod to attract attention.

clue.text: Six on eastern side watching television

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a wing is a side of a building or a team

explanation.surface: A group of six on the east flank are watching the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing a programme on screen is the act of looking at it.

clue.text: At home and away in billiards

parts.note: in means at home
off means away

explanation.surface: Playing at home and away games of billiards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home and away' suggests fixtures, but the definition is a shot in billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards stroke in which the cue ball goes into a pocket after striking another ball.

clue.text: At times one's life is in the balance

definitions.text: At times one's life is in the balance

parts.words: At times one's life is in the balance
parts.note: sounds like danger, but literally describes a performer balancing high up

explanation.surface: Sometimes someone's fate hangs uncertainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tumbler or tightrope performer whose safety depends on keeping their balance.

clue.text: Being tipsy as a result of this?

definitions.text: Being tipsy as a result of this?

indicators.note: tipsy implies the letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting drunk because of a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' rearranges BEING, and the whole clue also describes the answer, a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of heavy drinking leaves one drunk.

clue.text: Strong port, ours has been shaken

parts.note: Vigo is a port in northwest Spain

indicators.note: shaken means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Strong port wine, and our bottle has been shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine, but it is the Spanish port Vigo; 'has been shaken' rearranges OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic and robust, a synonym for powerful.

clue.text: Inside information that is given by a magical servant

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Secret information passed on by a magic helper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights, a spirit who serves whoever summons it, as from a lamp.

clue.text: Leave the circle to discuss another matter

definitions.text: Leave the circle to discuss another matter

parts.words: Leave the circle to discuss another matter
parts.note: a straight line touching a circle and heading away, read as wandering off topic

explanation.surface: Someone drifting away from the group to talk about something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to digress suddenly, from geometry, where a line touching a curve heads off in a new direction.
